protocol.title: PE beads · Exp 01 · Laser power from the MESF beads
protocol.summary: No power meter: the Quantum R-PE MESF beads are the power sensor. A laser-% ladder gives where PE stays linear, the signal per MESF per % for each objective, and (with Exp 02 and the simulator) the µW-equivalent of each %.

children.body: There is no power meter: the MESF beads are the power sensor, and the same read calibrates every plate.

attrs.title: Laser power from the MESF beads

chips.text: ≈1 h first time, 5 min per session after

children.body: Pins: where PE emission stops being linear in laser % (measured on PE itself at the real dwell, which is what the 1–2 µW rule stands in for); the signal per MESF per laser % for each objective (laser power and detection together, tracked every session); and, with DN per photoelectron from Exp 02 and the simulator's photon budget, the µW-equivalent of each laser %.

Model: in the linear regime the integrated signal F = k × MESF × (laser %). The simulator predicts ≈0.18 photoelectrons per PE per frame at 2 µW, 2 µs and 0.43 µm pixels through the 20x/0.80 (≈0.09 per µW), and F 5 % below linear near 5–6 µW; the review caps the operating point at 1–2 µW until Exp 07. One MESF is the emission of one R-PE molecule in solution, so the MESF beads read like PE on a bead, with the environment caveats of the MESF method.

Check on the Bangs certificate the bead size and whether the R-PE sits on the surface (a shell, like the capture beads) or through the bead (a disc). Image the MESF beads in the same mode and with the same plane rule as the capture beads; Exp 05 measures both focus curves.
≈1 h first time per objective; 5 min at the start and end of each quantitative session.

rows.free_text: Quantum R-PE MESF beads (Bangs): blank + 4 levels, lot MESF values from the certificate

children.body: Acquisition settings

rows.value: 20x (read the NA on the barrel), then the 10x/0.45 Plan Apo λD
One HV and offset for the whole ladder: the brightest level at the top rung below 80 % of full scale (stop the ladder lower rather than change the HV)
Galvano, 2 µs, 2048² at zoom 1, one frame per field

children.body: Before any quantitative acquisition: stand and lasers on for 2–3 h; 561 nm excitation; the same PE emission band (e.g. 570–620 nm) every time; 16-bit with fine integration (the default is 12-bit, so check the file); one HV and one offset for the whole session; background mode at least 50 DN above zero; no saturated pixels. Record the transmitted-light channel with every PE frame: beads are found in it, never in PE. Find focus in transmitted light and hold it with Perfect Focus. Never live-scan PE to focus.

attrs.label: From the MESF signal to a µW-equivalent

inputs.name: k_dn
inputs.label: Signal per MESF per laser % (fit of the ladder)

inputs.name: g_dn
inputs.label: DN per photoelectron at this HV (Exp 02)

inputs.name: e_uw
inputs.label: Simulator: photoelectrons per PE per frame per µW

inputs.name: target_uw
inputs.label: Operating point the simulations ask for

children.body: At [!var:k_dn] per MESF per % and [!var:g_dn] per photoelectron, 1 % laser is [!var:uw_pct] equivalent, so [!var:target_uw] needs [!var:pct_op] laser. The µW-equivalent rests on the simulator's collection and detector constants (±30–50 %); the linearity limit from the ladder is measured.
Set up
Laser on with the stand (the session's 2–3 h warm-up covers it). Vortex the MESF beads; one well per level plus the blank, as the kit says.

Settle the beads with a 1 min plate spin at 100–300 g. Find them and focus in transmitted light; hold focus with Perfect Focus at the capture beads' plane rule (the equator until Exp 05 gives the flat point).
Laser-% ladder (once per objective)
Set the HV and offset once, on the brightest level at the top rung (below 80 % of full scale). Do not change them during the ladder.
At each laser % (0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20), take one frame of a fresh field of every level and of the blank, ≥ 30 beads per level.
Repeat the 1 % rung at the end, to catch laser drift during the ladder.
Swap to the 10x and repeat.
A fresh field for every rung: a second frame on the same beads carries the first frame's bleaching (≈0.05 % per frame at 2 µW-equivalent, far more at the top rungs).
Every quantitative session

At the start and end of the session, image the MESF levels at the operating laser % (≥ 30 beads per level). The signal per MESF must stay within 5 % of this experiment's value; a larger change is laser or detector drift, and the plate is corrected with its own MESF slope. This read is also the plate's MESF calibration (Exp 10).
Per bead: integrated signal within R + 2.5 µm minus the background ring; median per level per rung; subtract the blank.

Linearity: signal against laser % on log–log axes, one line per level; fit the low rungs (slope 1). The rung where the signal falls 5 % below the line is PE's linearity limit through this objective. It should be the same % at every level; a level-dependent limit is detector non-linearity (check Exp 02).
Responsivity: over the linear rungs, fit signal = k × MESF × % across the levels (intercept at the blank). Record k, in DN per MESF per %, per objective with the HV used.

µW-equivalent: enter k, the DN per photoelectron at this HV (Exp 02) and the simulator's photoelectrons per PE per frame per µW in the calculator. Read the µW-equivalent of 1 % and the % for the operating point.
The 10x/20x ratio of k at the same % (back-aperture filling and collection together).

Decision: the operating laser % for each objective: at most half the linearity limit, and near the µW-equivalent the simulations ask for (1–2 through the 20x, ≈6 through the 10x), unless Exp 07 moves it. Every later protocol states power as this laser % with its µW-equivalent.
Record for every acquisition
